note.whiteDaysBody: The 13th, 14th, and 15th of each Islamic month fall around the full moon. Fasting these three bright days is a beloved sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ.
note.newMonthBody: The thin crescent (hilāl) marks the start of {{month}}. Each Islamic month begins when the new moon is first sighted after sunset.
note.fullBody: The moon is fully lit near the middle of {{month}} — the nights of the White Days, when fasting is especially recommended.
note.generalBody: The Islamic (Hijri) calendar follows the moon: every month is 29 or 30 days, beginning with the sighting of the new crescent.

about.duaBody: May Allah accept the efforts of everyone who contributed, forgive their shortcomings, and have mercy on their marhumeen. Ameen.
